svg.text: PETTY — where the keys come from, where they live, how they are used
Green = your device, memory only (never on disk). Yellow = a secret made on your device. Grey = server database (locked blobs + metadata only). Blue = a member's device.
users: email + Argon2id HASH of the login password
(proves who you are — touches no data)
(public; kept forever so old entries still verify)
Private keys exist in the clear only inside your device. A database thief holds two locked blobs and can only guess passphrases, about 1 second per guess.
IndexedDB keeps: key handles (24 h expiry),
Never a passphrase, a key, or decrypted data.
(who you are — not what you can read)
Wrap the drawer key for MY public key
AAD binds it to this drawer
Entry: signed with my ECDSA key,
then encrypted with the drawer key
entries: ciphertext + line id, seq, author, is_checkpoint
(never the amount, comment or line name)
READ: fetch my wrap → unwrap the drawer key with my private key
→ decrypt document + entries → verify every signature and the hash links
→ fold the balance. All of it in memory.
Invite: look up the member → compare their SAFETY NUMBER
(a fingerprint of their public keys) out of band → pin it
→ unwrap the drawer key → re-wrap it for THEIR public key
the invitation carries the wrap; on accept →
their device checks the sender against its PINNED key
→ same reads and writes as in 3
a NEW drawer key, wraps it for everyone left,
and re-encrypts the old rows. The old key
5 NEW DEVICE / LOST PASSPHRASE — keys are never regenerated
New device: login → the VAULT arrives
Lost passphrase AND recovery code, drawer shared with
nobody: unrecoverable, by design. Members of a shared
drawer can re-wrap its key for your new keypair.
